headline: GOLD CRATERS 2.6% TO $3,626 AS DOLLAR, FED SQUEEZE PRECIOUS METALS — Silver Falls 4.4% to $42.96; $3,500 Support Level Now in Focus
snippet: Spot gold fell 2.6% to $3,626.50 on November 20, extending the correction from August all-time highs as a strengthening US dollar and near-certain December Fed rate hike expectations created a rare dual headwind — geopolitical Iran tensions simultaneously strengthening the dollar instead of providing their usual safe-haven lift to gold. Silver fell harder at -4.4% to $42.96, tracking the equity-risk-asset selloff; gold is now approximately 13% below its year-to-date high and the $3,500 zone — where multiple central bank accumulation programs are expected to trigger sustained buying — is approaching as the next major technical support test for the entire mining equity complex.

headline: IVANHOE ELECTRIC DRILLS 123.6m AT 0.91% COPPER AT GLEESON ARIZONA — High-Grade Breccia Discovery Elevated to Highest Priority; Two Rigs Target 16,000m by Year-End
snippet: Ivanhoe Electric (TSX: IE) reported a breccia-hosted copper-gold-silver discovery at its Gleeson Project in southeastern Arizona on November 19, with the standout intercept of 123.6 metres at 0.91% copper, 0.44 g/t gold and 5.27 g/t silver from 601.7 metres depth — first significant drill results on private land 30 miles north of the historic Bisbee district. Management immediately elevated Gleeson to the company's highest exploration priority with two rigs now drilling toward a targeted 16,000 metres by year-end, while a second, deeper copper-gold-silver-zinc zone below 1,000 metres adds further dimension to what is a 500 by 500 metre footprint still open in all directions.

headline: COPPER LOSES $186B AS AI TRADE UNWINDS — China Yangshan Premium Hits Record $360/t While LME Futures Slide to 7-Month Lows
snippet: LME copper fell to a seven-month low near $5.58 per pound this week as AI-driven demand optimism and speculative tariff trades unwound simultaneously, wiping approximately $186 billion off the market capitalizations of the world's largest copper producers from their September peak. The selloff is producing a striking paradox: China's Yangshan copper import premium jumped roughly 20% to a record $360 per tonne — signalling physical demand is tight even as financial copper is sold aggressively — the same supply-demand disconnect that experienced copper investors use to identify cycle bottoms well before the futures market acknowledges them.

headline: DRUCKENMILLER DUMPS $120M GOOGLE STAKE, OPENS $43.9M NEWMONT POSITION — Also Buys Barrick, Agnico Eagle; Q3 13F Shows Macro Legend Rotating to Gold Miners
snippet: Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office Q3 2026 13F, filed November 16, shows the macro legend exited his entire $120 million Alphabet stake while opening new positions of approximately $43.9 million in Newmont, $42-43 million in Barrick Mining, and a similarly-sized stake in Agnico Eagle — allocating roughly 3% of the portfolio to gold miners just as the sector enters 52-week low territory. Gold miners fell 11-14% in the week following the filing as macro risk-off continues, posing the question retail investors evaluating the same sector are wrestling with: whether a legendary macro operator buying a dip that has since gone lower is early, or simply right on a longer timeframe than the current selling pressure implies.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING FINDS GOLD-SILVER IN ROCK CLASSED AS WASTE AT APOLLO — 15 of 17 Halo Holes Above Cut-Off Grade; $100M Colombia Budget Planned for 2027
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX-V: CNL) reported that 15 of 17 drill holes in the shallow halo surrounding the Apollo deposit in Colombia returned intervals above the open-pit cut-off grade — material classified as waste in the current mine plan — with the best intercept of 107.85 metres at 0.79 g/t gold and 14 g/t silver starting from just 3.75 metres depth. The discovery that Apollo's surrounding halo contains above-cut-off mineralization expands the resource footprint beyond the current model and, combined with the company's planned $100 million Colombian exploration budget for 2027, positions Apollo as one of the most capital-active junior exploration programs heading into next year.

headline: LITHIUM AMERICAS RAISES THACKER PASS CAPEX 31% TO $3.83B — Tariffs, Labour Inflation Add $900M; Trump Critical Minerals Drive Faces US Cost Reality
snippet: Lithium Americas (TSX/NYSE: LAC) raised Phase 1 capital costs for its Thacker Pass lithium project in Nevada by 31% to $3.83 billion — a $900 million increase driven by tariff impacts ($100M), craft labour wage inflation ($150M), piping and steel installation rate increases ($245M), and EPCM staffing costs ($250M) — creating a $995 million funding gap the company plans to plug through revised DOE loan arrangements. The cost blowout at Thacker Pass, one of the flagship projects of Trump-era domestic battery metals supply policy, signals that the structural challenge for US-based critical minerals ambitions isn't just permitting — it's the same inflation dynamics that have suppressed lithium miner valuations globally now hitting domestic greenfield construction head-on.

headline: USAR DIRECTOR BUYS $3M IN SHARES AFTER 37% MONTHLY DECLINE — Blitzer Acquires 450,000 Shares Nov 19 as Largest Insider Buy Since IPO
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) Director Michael Blitzer disclosed the purchase of 450,000 shares worth approximately $3 million on November 19 — the largest insider transaction since the company's 2026 public listing, made after USAR fell 37% over the prior month on a William Blair feedstock downgrade and broader sector profit-taking following the APEC-week Trump rare earth rally. While the purchase doesn't resolve the fundamental feedstock supply question that William Blair raised, it places a director's own capital at current levels alongside retail investors who bought the rare earth narrative — a signal sophisticated investors track as a risk-adjusted valuation marker even when institutional sentiment remains cautious.

headline: GENESIS-VAULT GOLD MERGER WINS WA SUPREME COURT APPROVAL — Combined Entity to Become Australia's Third-Largest Gold Producer at 600-700Koz/yr
snippet: The Supreme Court of Western Australia approved the Genesis-Vault gold merger scheme on November 17, with Vault shares suspended from the ASX at close of trading and the combined entity expected to begin trading as Australia's third-largest gold producer with annual production guidance of 600,000-700,000 ounces. The court approval closes as ASX gold equities have been among the hardest-hit in the global mining selloff — putting the new combined company under immediate pressure to demonstrate that the operational synergies and production scale that justified the deal can deliver value at current gold prices, the core test for consolidation-driven M&A in any depressed commodity cycle.

headline: SCORPION MINERALS ACQUIRES 289 sq km PAYNES FIND GOLD PROJECT WA — Binding Deal Signed Nov 19 for District-Scale Exploration Target Near Infrastructure
snippet: Scorpion Minerals (ASX: SCN) signed a binding agreement on November 19 to acquire 100% of the Paynes Find Gold Project in Western Australia — a 289 square kilometre holding in a historically producing gold district northeast of Perth with established infrastructure access and multiple drill-ready targets. At a time when TSX-V and ASX junior acquirers have largely stepped back from project acquisitions in the gold selloff, Scorpion's move signals management confidence that current pricing represents the right window to build land position in an established WA gold corridor ahead of an eventual sector recovery.

headline: GOLD'S LOSING STREAK PUTS 10 MINING STOCKS ON OVERSOLD WATCHLIST — Down 13% YTD; Gold Reserve and Contango Silver Are Only Names With RSI Below 30
snippet: Seeking Alpha flagged 10 mining stocks hitting technically oversold territory as spot gold falls to 52-week lows, down approximately 13% year-to-date, with Gold Reserve and Contango Silver & Gold the only names in the screened universe showing RSI readings below 30 — the threshold that historically precedes mean-reversion bounces in cyclical commodity equities. The oversold designation doesn't guarantee a bottom, but for retail investors building positions through a selloff rather than timing it perfectly, the RSI screen identifies where the most compressed names are — the high-risk/high-reward layer of a gold mining allocation where entry timing matters most and the gap between intrinsic value and current price is widest.
